actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.

At the conclusion of debate, the chair put the question on the motion to suspend the rules. Mr. Bost objected to the vote on the grounds that a quorum was not present. Further proceedings on the motion were postponed. The point of no quorum was considered as withdrawn.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 1969.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H2175-2177; text: CR H2175-2176)
Mr. Bost moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended.
Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 76.

dimensions.assessment: Affects veterans, members of the Armed Forces, their families, and participating health care providers and grant recipients.
dimensions.evidence: provide or coordinate suicide prevention services for veterans and members of the Armed Forces and their families

dimensions.assessment: Modifies clinical screening protocols, creates mandatory notification and care procedures for emergent suicide care, and expands grant eligibility to include health care providers.
dimensions.evidence: baseline mental health screenings for risk provided as suicide prevention services under the program to use a protocol selected by the VA

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes $52,500,000 specifically for fiscal year 2026 for the grant program.
Amends existing statutory provisions governing the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program and veterans' medical services.
dimensions.evidence: To amend and reauthorize the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs

dimensions.assessment: Extends program duration through fiscal year 2026 and adjusts specific benefit and pension payment limits to 2033.

missing_information: Long-term funding authorizations beyond fiscal year 2026 for the grant program.
importance_detail.rationale: Reauthorizes and modifies a VA suicide prevention grant program with an additional $52.5 million for fiscal year 2026, expands eligible entities, updates screening protocols, and alters veterans' care requirements.
